output.title: What folder structure usually hides in a small business
output.body:
For an owner-operator, messy folders usually hide a simpler problem: repeated document search. If you keep hunting for customer agreements, invoices, contracts, or past decisions, the folder tree is not the workflow. It is where the friction shows up.

The real question is not, “How do I reorganise everything?” It is, “Is there one repeated document task that is worth automating later, once I understand it clearly?” That might be invoice filing, contract retrieval, or answering a customer query from old files. This is a threshold decision, not a full system rebuild.

A practical next step is manual: pick your most common lookup for one week and write down three things each time it happens. What were you looking for? Which folders did you check? How long did it take before you found it, or gave up and asked someone else? That small audit tells you whether you have occasional clutter or a recurring process.

If the same lookup keeps coming back and costs real time, you may have a workflow worth tightening. If it is ad hoc or takes seconds, the folder structure may be annoying, but not yet a business process. Folder names are often the smoke, not the fire.
